findings.reason: a node whose second deliverable its own done-when cannot fail on is one deliverable plus a spare, and splitting it (investigation node, fix node) or extending the done-when to require the recorded finding changes the node graph.
findings.text: §2 opens "**Deliverable.** First, an investigation … Then make the reflex launch a review whenever a run settles at a head that no stored review is keyed to", but the done-when only asserts the reflex's launch behaviour and never measures the investigation's recorded output, so the node carries an unmeasured deliverable

findings.reason: the rubric's third reasoning check requires the caller be named, and here the un-named caller is load-bearing: a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk §5 landed claiming "A runtime-source move earns a light re-review of those commits", so a node told to "make the reflex launch a review whenever a run settles at a head that no stored review is keyed to" may re-implement logic that is already present instead of finding why the present logic does not fire, sending the repair at the wrong mechanism.
findings.text: §2 names no module and no caller, writing only "Write paths: the reflex's module, named by the investigation", while the mechanism it asks for already exists and runs: `dispatch_review_for_run` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1279) calls `review_head_move` (:726) and `carry_review_forward` (:1426), and is reached from the watch path (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:2423)

findings.reason: the section's own evidence shows the merged head carrying a review, so the root-cause sentence "the head that merges goes unreviewed unless the coordinator notices" is supported only if those reviews were hand-dispatched and not reflex-launched; the plan must distinguish reflex-launched from hand-dispatched reviews (e.g. from the run's `review_dispatch` record) or the premise the whole plan rests on is unevidenced by the anchors it cites.
findings.text: §1 asserts the resumed runs "were reviewed only at the old head", but the review store holds a review at every cited moved head — `71bb011d8f3c4e5d32035d35c71989b56c5b2b4b` for structural-guards-have-one-home, `2cf592a5571a993074c6b70f2e2ba1b69a996e88` and `3fa0ce0efe343fbfc99f99ac3ddf1bdd0ab5adc1` for gc-bounds-a-run-file, `624314887fde13d8026103bad40c8fcd717163cc` for dispatch-names-the-health-review

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited commit resolves (`c47c99ef6`, `71bb011d8`, `92d3ec6ca`, `2cf592a55`, `3fa0ce0ef`, `29185a66a`, `624314887`), the node ids resolve to stored review records under `docs/state/reckon/reviews/run/`, and `a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk#s5` resolves and reads as §1 quotes it.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2's done-when is measurable and names a negative control that fires: with the review lookup ignoring `reviewed_head_sha`, the resumed run at head B gets no review and the test fails.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the investigation is recorded in the run directory and the gate is the named test file; neither lands in a session scratchpad or node-local temp path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach a symbol; `reviewed_head_sha` and `tests/test_a_moved_head_is_reviewed.py` are mechanism-named.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the reflex's moved-head re-review mechanism already exists and is reached, and §1's central evidence (the moved heads "reviewed only at the old head") is contradicted by the review store.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §2 declares two deliverables, a recorded investigation and the reflex fix, and its single done-when measures only the fix.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan's `plan-informs` target `a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk` exists and its §5 is the rule §1 says it extends; no `depends-on` or `gates` is declared, and none is owed now that the sibling §5 has landed.
